heard.who: World Health Organization, health topic page on smallpox
heard.quote: In 1980 WHO declared smallpox eradicated - the only infectious disease to achieve this distinction.

answer: Yes. Smallpox was eradicated from the world in 1980, and the last known natural case had been in Somalia in 1977.

facts.text: Smallpox was eradicated from the world in 1980.

sources.title: History of smallpox vaccination
sources.quote: In 1980, WHO declared smallpox officially eradicated : The world and all its people have won freedom from smallpox

sources.publisher: Bulletin of the World Health Organization (W. H. Foege)
sources.title: Commentary: smallpox eradication in west and central Africa revisited
sources.quote: In May 1980, the Thirty-third World Health Assembly adopted a resolution accepting the report of the Global Commission for the Certification of Smallpox Eradication and affirming its belief that this once-universal disease had been eradicated worldwide

sources.title: The world defeated smallpox. Why does polio still exist?
sources.quote: On May 8, 1980, the World Health Organization announced that, for the first time, a human infectious disease had been completely eradicated.

facts.text: The last known natural case of smallpox was Ali Maow Maalin, a health worker in Somalia, in 1977.

sources.title: Ali Maow Maalin Survives the Last Endemic Smallpox Case
sources.quote: The last known case of endemic (naturally-occurring) smallpox occurred in Merka, Somalia, in 1977

sources.title: World Health Organization Intensifies Its Campaign to Eradicate Smallpox
sources.quote: The last case of variola minor was reported in Somalia on October 26, 1977.

sources.title: The world defeated smallpox. Why does polio still exist?
sources.quote: Ali Maow Maalin had been the last person to be infected by the naturally occurring form

contested.text: Whether the last stocks of live variola virus should be destroyed. WHO describes a lengthy and complex debate over this since eradication.

sources.title: Smallpox
sources.quote: The period since eradication has been defined by a lengthy and complex debate focussed on the destruction of the last remaining stocks of live variola virus.
